---
title: Get started
description: "Build, run, and export a small study in about ten minutes. Nothing to install."
---

Ten minutes, one browser tab, nothing to install: consent, one task, a completion code.

## 1. Open the modeler

[Open the modeler](https://behaverse.org/studyflow-modeler/app.html), press <kbd>⌘K</kbd> (<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> on Windows and Linux), and choose **New...**, then **Empty diagram**.

Rename the study **Minimal study** in the toolbar.

::: {.callout-tip}
Nothing leaves your browser until you export, publish, or switch run recording on.
:::

## 2. Add the task

From **Activities** in the palette, drag **Cognitive Task** right of the start event; double-click it and name it **Flanker**.

![Dragging an activity from the palette onto the canvas, next to the start event.](../assets/img/screenshots/3-drag.png){#fig-drag fig-alt="A start event on the canvas with a task-shaped outline being dropped to its right, a horizontal blue alignment guide running through both."}

In the inspector, set **Instrument** to `jsPsych` (**General** tab) and **Implementation** (**Execution** tab) to:

```
https://github.com/jspsych/jspsych-contrib@v0.4.0#flanker
```

## 3. Connect the elements

Hover the start event and drag the arrow from its toolbar onto the task.

Then drag **End** out of **Events** and connect the task to it.

## 4. Simulate

Click **Simulate**: a *token* --- one dot per participant --- leaves the start event and follows your arrows.

![A token travelling the flow during a simulation.](../assets/img/screenshots/8-simulate.png){#fig-simulate fig-alt="A start, task, end flow during simulation, with a magenta token filling the start event."}

Simulation checks that your arrows connect.

## 5. Run it

Click **Run**. The browser runner opens in a second tab, checks the study, then walks you through three screens:

![The browser runner asking for informed consent, because the start event carries a consent form address.](../assets/img/runner/consent.png){#fig-consent fig-alt="A participant-facing screen titled Enrollment showing an informed consent form with Decline and I consent buttons."}

| Screen | Comes from | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| Informed consent | `consentFormUri` on the start event | read the form, then choose *I consent* |
| Flanker | the task, with the software it names | press *Continue* |
| Study complete | `redirectTo` and `completionCodeType` on the end event | copy the code, or let it send you back --- the code is generated for this run and substituted into the redirect, which is how a panel credits the participant |

![The final screen: a completion code, and the address the participant is sent back to.](../assets/img/runner/completion.png){#fig-completion fig-alt="A screen titled Study complete showing a generated completion code and a five-second countdown to a redirect URL."}

The **Logs** panel lists every step it took.

::: {.callout-note}
The browser runner shows the Flanker step and the software it names. The consent form is fetched from the address on the start event; clear that field to skip the screen.
:::

## 6. Export the file

Open **Export...**, choose **PNG**, and leave **Studyflow source** on. Then open the downloaded file with **Open File...** — the study comes back, fully editable.

The image is not a screenshot of the study. It *is* the study, with the full source riding inside the file.

| Export as | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `.studyflow.png` or `.studyflow.svg` | a figure that opens back up as the editable study |
| `.studyflow.yaml` | the canonical text form: reading, reviewing, version control |

## The whole study {#the-whole-study}

Exporting as **Studyflow** gives the same study as text ([File format](../reference/file-format.qmd)).

```yaml
id: minimal_study
definitions:
  targetNamespace: http://bpmn.io/schema/bpmn

Minimal_Study:
  type: bpmn:Process
  name: Minimal study
  extensionElements:
    - type: studyflow:Study
  flowElements:

    Enrolled:
      type: bpmn:StartEvent
      name: Enrolled and consented
      consentFormUri: https://example.org/protocols/minimal-study/consent.md

    Flanker:
      type: bpmn:Task
      name: Flanker
      extensionElements:
        - type: cognitive:CognitiveTask
          instrument: jspsych
          implementation: https://github.com/jspsych/jspsych-contrib@v0.4.0#flanker

    Done:
      type: bpmn:EndEvent
      name: Done
      redirectTo: https://app.prolific.com/submissions/complete?cc={COMPLETION_CODE}
      completionCodeType: dynamic

    Flow_Enrolled_Flanker:
      type: bpmn:SequenceFlow
      sourceRef: Enrolled
      targetRef: Flanker
    Flow_Flanker_Done:
      type: bpmn:SequenceFlow
      sourceRef: Flanker
      targetRef: Done
```

Every line is something you set in the editor: [minimal_study.studyflow.yaml](../assets/examples/minimal_study.studyflow.yaml).

## Beyond the minimum

- **Ask a question first.** Put a **Questionnaire** before the task and set its **Instrument** to `PHQ-9`; the runner shows the nine items and records the answers.
- **Randomize the order of two tasks.** Add a second task, drag **Random** out of **Gateways**, and draw one branch per order. [Randomize and counterbalance](../design/randomization.qmd) covers the balanced variants.
- **Keep the data.** Recording is off by default: switch on **Record events** in the runner's log panel, or **Record run data** under **Settings → Privacy**. [Data](../reference/data.qmd) says what is stored.

![A standard questionnaire, rendered by the browser runner from the instrument you picked.](../assets/img/runner/questionnaire.png){#fig-questionnaire fig-alt="The PHQ-9 questionnaire rendered as nine prompts, each with four response buttons, and a Submit button."}
